title: 20 Goals, Zero Conceded: India U17 Women Storm Into Back-to-Back Asian Cups
excerpt: A 4-0 win over Malaysia sealed a perfect Group E campaign for the Young Tigresses, making them the first Indian side at any age level to qualify for consecutive Women's Asian Cups.
body:
• India's U17 women's team beat hosts Malaysia 4-0 in Selayang on October 11 to top Group E and qualify for the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup China 2027.
  • The Young Tigresses finished the qualifiers with a perfect record: three wins, 20 goals scored and zero conceded — including a record 14-0 demolition of Iraq.
  • They are now the first Indian side at any age level, including the senior teams, to qualify for back-to-back Women's Asian Cups.
  • For diaspora fans: 15-year-old striker Anushka Kumari scored 8 of India's 20 goals; the finals in China run from March 31 to April 17, 2027.

A perfect campaign sealed in Selayang

India's U17 women's football team made history on Sunday, defeating hosts Malaysia 4-0 in their final Group E match at the MP Selayang Stadium to qualify for the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup China 2027. The result capped a flawless qualifying campaign — nine points from three matches, 20 goals scored, and not a single one conceded.

Redima Devi Chingkhamayum broke the deadlock in the 29th minute with a powerful right-footed strike off a pass from Silky Devi Sorokhaibam, after India had dominated possession and won nine first-half corners on a rain-soaked, slushy pitch. Malaysian goalkeeper Putri Aina Husna Binto Mohd Subri had kept the hosts in the contest with a string of saves, including denying Nira Chanu Longjam's header and clearing an Anushka Kumari effort off the line. After the break, substitute Pritika Barman doubled the lead, Anushka added a third with her eighth goal of the qualifying campaign, and substitute Nidhi completed the rout with her first-ever international goal — a solo run from 25 yards that weaved past three defenders before rounding the goalkeeper.

Context & Background

India's campaign began on October 5 with a staggering 14-0 demolition of Iraq — the biggest-ever win by an Indian U17 women's team — in which Anushka scored five goals. A disciplined 2-0 victory over Syria followed, with Anushka scoring both. Malaysia had opened with a 1-0 win over Syria before thrashing Iraq 4-0, setting up Sunday's encounter as a straight contest for the group's single qualifying spot: only the eight group winners advance from the qualifiers.

This is the second consecutive qualification for the Young Tigresses, who reached the quarter-finals of the AFC U17 Women's Asian Cup China 2026 — the first time any Indian team had progressed to the knockout stage of the competition. Thirteen players from that squad, including captain Abhista Basnett, goalkeeper Munni and Anushka, returned for this cycle, giving Alexandersson's group a core of proven experience under pressure.

At the finals in China, India will join defending champions DPR Korea, Japan, Australia and hosts China PR, who qualified directly after finishing among the top four at the 2026 edition, plus the seven other group winners from qualifying.

Impact & Analysis

The numbers tell the story of a team operating at a different level than its qualifying opposition: 20 goals for, none against, across opponents who themselves had managed clean sheets and convincing wins. But the deeper significance is structural. No Indian team — men's or women's, senior or youth — had ever reached consecutive Asian Cup editions before. Women's football in India has historically battled for resources, visibility and continuity; a back-to-back qualification achieved on the back of a settled squad and a long-term coach is evidence that the youth development pathway is beginning to hold together across cycles rather than resetting every tournament.

The defensive record deserves as much attention as the goals. Clean sheets against three different styles of opposition, including a disciplined Malaysian side playing at home, suggest a team that can manage matches — not just win shootouts. That maturity, carried over by 13 returning players who have already experienced an Asian Cup knockout round, is what gives this group a credible chance of improving on its quarter-final finish in China.

"Even if people outside think we are the favourites, we must always stay humble, whoever we are facing. In every sport, you have to be humble and respect the opponent."

— Joakim Alexandersson, India U17 women's head coach

What's Next

India's focus now shifts to the finals in China, scheduled from March 31 to April 17, 2027. The draw and group-stage fixtures will be announced in due course, with the Young Tigresses aiming to go beyond the 2026 quarter-final — the nation's best-ever performance at the tournament. A full breakdown of India's qualifying campaign underlines how central continuity has been to this run. Whether this generation can convert qualifying dominance into a deep run against Asia's elite — DPR Korea, Japan, Australia — will be the defining test of the program's progress.
